chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

The Mutamatti' (pilgrim who performs Umrah then Hajj) if he arrives on the night of Arafah, there is no 'Umrah for him that he makes a separate Hajj; rather, the 'Umrah is only until the Day of Tarwiyah.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah and then Hajj in the same season, combining them.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: The night preceding the Day of Arafah, a key time for Hajj rituals.
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Here referring to the Umrah ritual performed separately before Hajj.
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th day of Dhul-Hijjah, traditionally when pilgrims proceed to Mina.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who enters Ihram for Hajj on the night of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundary of the Umrah component for a Mutamatti', stipulating that if one delays entering Ihram for Hajj until the night of Arafah, the Umrah period effectively ends at the Day of Tarwiyah. This ruling ensures the distinct separation of the two rites, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence, preventing the conflation of Umrah and Hajj when the transition is delayed. It underscores the precision required in timing the transition from the state of Ihram for Umrah to that for Hajj.
